_comment: Production balancing (Homestead's own values, not taken from the original). Times in game seconds. Workshop inputs/outputs must match the building's request/offer piles in data/buildings. Mines eat food from their input piles (see mineFood). Gatherers: workSeconds at the spot, restSeconds at home, pickupSeconds a pause before picking up what they got (the woodcutter after felling).

mineFood._comment: Trips into the mine one unit of food lasts: the mine's prefersFood lasts preferredRuns trips, any other food otherRuns. pileCapacity: units each food pile of a mine holds. freeRuns: trips into a new mine that cost no food (per building, so a rebuilt mine gets them again).

distribution._comment: Defaults of Waren > Verteilung: how a material is shared among the targets that use it (shares 0-1 by building name, "construction" for construction sites; listed materials give unlisted targets 0, unlisted materials give every target 1). Among the targets that want it now, the target is drawn by share, then the nearest of that kind with room gets it; share 0 gets nothing, unless the player set every target of the material to 0. Storehouses last.
distribution._cropWaterComment: Without a rule the nearest user takes it all: a mill next to the farm would leave the brewery dry.

trade._comment: Land trade. The donkey farm makes a donkey (a figure, not a good) of its farmInputs every farmSeconds while the player has fewer than keepIdle donkeys without a job. Markets: carriers bring the goods the player chose in the market's panel, then the nearest free donkey fetches up to load units (loadSeconds each to load or unload) and carries them along the route to the destination. sight: how far a donkey sees in the fog of war (little, so it cannot scout).

shipping._comment: Shipyards first need a dock: the player clicks into the water, the pier (dockLength fields of open water, straight out from a free shore field) goes at once where its end is nearest the click, within dockDistance of the shipyard on own land.
shipping._shipsComment: One ship at a time on a shipyard's stocks: carriers bring its cost, the worker carries unit by unit along the pier and hammers each in for buildSeconds. Costs guessed, not measured in the original. passengers: units (soldiers, priests, geologists, scouts, pioneers) it takes aboard. stepSeconds: a ship from one field to the next; sight: how far it sees. landingDistance: land at most this far from a ship is near enough to board and to unload.

smiths._comment: One product per cycle: what the player ordered (Waren > Herstellung) first, then tools somebody waits for (and nobody has), otherwise by shares (the player's bars, these are the defaults; 0 = only on order or need) while the product has fewer than keepInStock units around (0 = no limit); otherwise the smith rests. The toolsmith makes only what is needed right now unless the player gives it shares.

recruitment._comment: Share of a player's carriers and specialists (soldiers not counted) that always stays carriers: no carrier becomes a specialist or soldier below it. Living houses bring new ones. maxDiggers/maxBuilders: most diggers/builders as a share of the same count (at least one each). All three are the defaults of Siedler > Berufe, where the player changes them.

tools._comment: Tool a carrier must take to become the trade (game knowledge, as in JSettlers' EMovableType). BLADE is the digger's shovel.

placement._comment: Fields a new building keeps free from the ground and the surroundings of other buildings (more room for settlers and the looks; 0 = touching allowed as in the original data).

levelling._comment: Levelling a construction site: its footprint goes to its mean height, and around it the ground is cut or filled ring by ring until no neighbor differs by more than maxSlope (99 % of the original terrain stays within 7). Work is the height moved in all; a place needing more than maxWork cannot be built on. Diggers move a point by heightPerDig per work cycle, never making a slope steeper than maxSlope, so on a hillside they start at the top.

storage._comment: Units per storehouse pile; a storehouse has six piles, each holding one material at a time. A full storehouse takes nothing more: goods then wait at the producers.
storage._materialsComment: Defaults of Waren > Warentransport. materials: what carriers bring to storehouses; everything else stays at its producer (output pile of 8; the producer waits when it is full) and is fetched from there when needed. transportOrder: which goods carriers take first (goods not listed come last).

housing._comment: Carriers a finished living house sends out through its door, one every intervalSeconds. Houses that come with a loaded map do not (the map lists its settlers itself).

demolition._comment: Share of the construction material a building leaves on the ground when it is torn down or lost with its land (construction sites: of the material already built in). 0.5 as in JSettlers.

crops._comment: What farm-like gatherers sow and harvest: growSeconds from sowing to ripe, on these grounds. regrows: starts over after the harvest instead of leaving free ground (vines, beehives). slopeBonus: grows up to (1 + slopeBonus) times as fast where the height to a neighbor differs by slopeHeight or more (vines on hillsides). farmland: sowing turns the grass into farmland (drawn as earth), which stays until the farm is torn down or lost; farmlandRadius: also the free grass that many steps around (where farmland fits).

walking._comment: Walking speed by ground, for every settler: trailSpeed times as fast on a trail, mountainSpeed times on mountains (Mountain, MountainBorder). A trail forms on plain grass where carriers on a job stepped trailSteps times, each step less than trailFadeSeconds after the one before; a trail nobody walked on for trailFadeSeconds fades.

resources._comment: Mountains and waters: a field of the original maps holds an amount of 0-15 (mostly 8). orePerAmount/fishPerAmount = units per amount step, so a mine's stock scales with it. regenerateSeconds: a depleted field regains one step this often (0 = never). fullAmount: a mine's chance per run is the ore left within its radius against fullAmount on every field there (empty fields and other resources are misses; a miss costs the run and its food), so every find lowers it; 0 = every run hits while ore is left.

geologists._comment: A geologist sent to a mountain searches field after field within searchRadius of that point: surveySeconds examining, signSeconds setting the sign. A sign shows what lies below and how much, and disappears after signMinutes (random between the two values). Values from JSettlers' GeologistMovable and RessourceSignMapObject (MIT), radius our own.

depletion._comment: Our own balancing: percent of the units taken that use up the ground. stone: quarry stone; mountain: everything mines dig (coal, ores, gems, sulfur); fish. 100 as in the original, e.g. 75, 50, 25, 10; 0 = never runs out.
